claims.text: Language models are highly sensitive to epistemic markers in prompts.
Accuracies of language models vary by more than 80% based on the epistemic markers used in prompts.
Expressions of high certainty result in a 7% decrease in accuracy compared to low certainty expressions.
Factive verbs hurt language model performance.
Markers of uncertainty are associated with answers on question-answering websites in pretraining data.
Markers of certainty are associated with questions on question-answering websites in pretraining data.
Language model behavior regarding epistemic markers may be based on mimicking observed language use rather than reflecting epistemic uncertainty.

evidence.description: We find that LMs are highly sensitive to epistemic markers in prompts, with accuracies varying more than 80%.
Surprisingly, we find that expressions of high certainty result in a 7% decrease in accuracy as compared to low certainty expressions.
Our analysis of a popular pretraining dataset shows that these markers of uncertainty are associated with answers on question-answering websites.

methodologies.name: Epistemic Marker Injection
methodologies.description: Development of a typology of epistemic markers and injection of 50 markers into prompts for question answering tasks.

limitations.text: Behavior of LMs may be based on mimicking observed language use, rather than truly reflecting epistemic uncertainty.
